goal: Make the game's interface feel like a high-quality adventure game (Zelda-tier), not a generic web overlay. The last pass added a gold hairline to every surface, but a hairline around a rectangle is still a rectangle — the HUD still reads as web chrome. Now give the surfaces real SHAPE and hierarchy: the crystal counter should be a shaped badge/crest (an inline SVG frame or clip-path silhouette with notched or scrolled corners), menu panels should be shaped plaques rather than rounded rects, and the primary button should read as a carved/gilded plate — its current cyan gradient also clashes with the gold fantasy palette, so bring it into the palette. Retire the debug FPS chip from the default HUD (put it behind ?fps or ?debug) and make the control legend introduce itself then fade out of the way instead of parking on screen for the whole session. Prefer inline SVG frames drawn once and reused over piles of CSS pseudo-elements. Each iteration, pick the single highest-impact surface and lift it properly rather than touching everything shallowly. Keep it readable in motion over a bright 3D scene. Hard rules: never weaken, skip or delete a test to make the gate pass; never loosen the thresholds or checks in scripts/ui-gate.mjs, scripts/visual-gate.mjs or tests/perf.spec.js; do not raise the draw-call/triangle budget; the UI must keep working on the plain mobile render path and stay within the 44px touch floor; do not add a runtime dependency or a webfont beyond the two already bundled.
_note: Command gate only, on purpose. A machine cannot judge whether a UI 'feels like Zelda' -- that is taste, and per docs/GATES.md it belongs to a human. What the gate CAN do is hold a craft floor so the loop cannot call generic default styling done: scripts/ui-gate.mjs asserts every major surface carries a real frame treatment (ornament layer / border-image / clip-path / mask, NOT just border-radius+blur), the display face is actually applied, touch targets clear 44px, nothing overflows at 320/390/768/1280, iconography exists, and text on solid surfaces clears 4.5:1. It was checked against the current UI and fails with 8 violations that match the complaint. Its contrast check deliberately skips gradient-backed text rather than report a false failure. Passing this gate means the floor is met, NOT that the UI is beautiful -- run with --human-gate to judge that.

command_gate.command: pnpm build && pnpm test && node scripts/visual-gate.mjs && node scripts/ui-gate.mjs
